scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: zero point one plus zero point two
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Zero point one plus zero point two should be zero point three. Python prints zero point three, then a long tail ending in four. This is not a Python mistake. Computers store decimals in binary, and some decimals cannot be stored exactly. So round the answer before you show it, and you get a clean zero point three.

props.why: Computers store decimals in binary, so some decimals are stored as close values, not exact ones; round before showing a result.

shorts.title: Two kinds of numbers
shorts.script: Python has two kinds of numbers. An int is a whole number, like three fish. A float has a decimal point, like one hundred twenty and a half rupees. You can mix them in one sum, and Python gives you a float whenever a float is in the sum. Whole things get ints, and measured things get floats. Simple as that. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: int and float in 40 seconds.

shorts.title: Division is a float
shorts.script: A small surprise. Ten divided by two is five, but Python prints five point zero. Division with a single slash always gives a float, even when the answer looks whole. That is on purpose. A division can give a decimal, so Python always gives a float. Remember it when you print. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Slash always gives a float.

shorts.title: What is type?
shorts.hook: "The type function tells you the type of the object that a name points at."
shorts.script: The type function tells you the type of the object that a name points at. Type of three says int. Type of one hundred twenty and a half says float. The type belongs to the value, not to the name. So the same name can point at an int now, and a float later. Use type whenever you are unsure what you are holding. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Check the type.

shorts.title: Point one plus point two
shorts.hook: "Zero point one plus zero point two is not zero point three in Python."
shorts.script: Zero point one plus zero point two is not zero point three in Python. It prints zero point three, then a long tail ending in four. Computers store decimals in binary, and some decimals cannot be stored exactly. It is not a bug in Python. The fix is easy. Round the answer to two places before you show it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Floats are close, not exact.
